dataset.name: IBM AMLworld HI-Small (synthetic), 10-day slice cut by us
notes: Four ring units (u15 mesh, u26 scatter-gather, u49 cycle, u50 fan-in) have most of their labeled rows after 2022-09-10, in the file's tail where 59 percent of rows are labeled; a late timestamp is a tell there (R155).
Every laundering transfer in this slice is ACH; in the whole file it is 87 percent (R155).
Slice laundering rate 4.0 percent vs 0.10 percent in the file; labels are IBM's generator's; shape names are ours.

Every one of the 40 ordinary neighborhoods contains an account that sits in one of IBM's rings (the slice was cut around the rings), so a 'false ring' at the transfer level usually points at a real laundering account's unlabeled traffic; account_level reports that view.

versions.v1: model reads the raw transfers of a neighborhood
versions.v2: code computes the neighborhood's facts (degrees, loops, bursts, pass-through chains, formats) and the model names the outcome
versions.v3: v2 plus a real knowledge-base lookup of the pattern reference, logged as the retrieval step
versions.v4: v3 plus a rule: keep a ring call only at medium or high confidence
versions.v5: v3 with a framing that states the base rate, describes ordinary business, requires a cited fact and allows cannot tell
versions.v2x: v2 with the payment format hidden from the model, to measure reliance on the ACH tell

runs.why: Account 80F181A50 receives 9 repeated, near-identical Swiss Franc payments from 100428978 (103.17 and 148.63 alternating, Sep 2 to Sep 10) and forwards repeated 103.88 payments to 80FA97F90, which looks like pass-through layering, with 80E613530 adding one inflow (T0888). The amounts do not reconcile hop by hop, and recurring fixed payments can be ordinary, so this needs review rather than a conclusion. T2299 (0.01 from 80F742460) may be a probe but is excluded because the evidence is thin.

Account 802E8B2A0 receives small inflows (T0166 388.70 from 802E8AE50, T2417 40.11 from 80044E450) and then sends 164,253.39 (T0695) and 214,602.61 (T2402) to 81309A8F0, so the outflows far exceed anything visible in this set and the source of those funds is unexplained. This is a referral-worthy layering shape, but the neighborhood also shows recurring identical-amount payments that could be ordinary bills, and no cycle or closed loop appears, so this needs source-of-funds review before any conclusion.

Account 8009636A0 sends 12 outbound transfers over 9 days to several counterparties, repeating identical amounts (12046.47 three times, 22944.38 twice, 31.24 four times) and funneling large sums to 800EA4CC0, which then pays 802A32F30. There is no round trip back to the origin, and recurring identical payments can be ordinary, so this needs review of the customer relationships before any conclusion.

Account 8113348B0 receives 14 transfers from 810C151B0 in about 10 days, all in Shekels, using only two repeated amounts (1935.12 and 1346.02), some sent late at night. It also receives two large transfers (147,088.38 and 410,132.05) from 800948490, which is itself a hub that also pays out to two other accounts. The repetition and convergence fit a fan-in, but the pattern could be ordinary recurring payments, and no cycle or layering is visible, so this warrants review rather than a conclusion of laundering.

Account 80043DF50 receives large inbound transfers from 800259050 (T0271, T0839, T1486) and then disperses funds across at least six counterparties, with repeated identical amounts (e.g., 1208.56 to 80D3EA400 three times, 6474.5 to 8018F3490 twice, 1788.68 to 802E343B0 twice, 57.25 to 8025DA150 twice) over a few days, which looks like a pass-through hub rather than ordinary activity. Confidence is only medium because recurring fixed payments such as bills or subscriptions could produce the same pattern, and the data includes no account-holder context or onward-flow visibility to rule that out.

Account 800957210 fans out to four recipient accounts with many repeated identical amounts (e.g. 1329.71 four times to 806790ED0, 7928.27 twice to 800DFCC20, 147.9 twice to 807483A20), and 807A374E0 receives from the hub and from 803A8FF70 before sending 1,005,868.51 in cash to 810C93920 (T1600), which looks like a consolidate-and-cash-out step. Confidence is medium because a busy hub with recurring fixed payments could be legitimate, and T0252/T2089 (identical 96,587.47 from 100428660) may be a duplicate record rather than a separate transfer; I did not flag those.

Account 80F1AF380 sends 12 transfers in about four days (Sep 1 to Sep 4) to 12 distinct accounts across several banks and currencies, ranging from about 3.6k to 278k, which is a fan-out layering shape. There are no return flows to the origin and no onward forwarding visible in this set, and several recurring fixed-amount flows elsewhere look like standing payments, so this could be ordinary treasury or payroll disbursement and needs KYC and business-purpose review before any conclusion.

Account 8100920E0 receives repeated, identical large inflows from 80FF95550 (cash-format 32,922,640.04 three times, plus 29,735.31 twice) and a 50,878.02 transfer from 808C30740, then disperses funds across roughly seven recipient accounts in many smaller and mid-sized payments. Identical repeated amounts could equally be duplicate postings or recurring payments, so this needs verification against source records before any escalation.

Account 8009D3030 receives ACH credits from three accounts (T1389, T1391, T1392, about 31.6k EUR total) and then, within about 4 days, pays out ACH in five currencies (Yuan, Yen, Ruble, Peso, USD, Euro) to seven different accounts (T1653, T1741, T1750, T1860, T1972, T2210, T2664), a pattern consistent with layering through a pass-through hub. Money does not return to its origin, the outflows are much larger than the inflows, and the data cannot show the purpose of these transfers, so this could be ordinary business activity; the repeated identical-amount transfers elsewhere (e.g., 802B99D60 to

Twelve transfers from 12 different originating accounts at 12 different banks all land on 80D7FBC70 within about 28 minutes on the night of 2022-09-10, which is a classic collection pattern. Legitimate explanations such as a business or merchant collection account are possible, so this warrants review rather than a conclusion; T0462 is excluded because it goes to a different account at a different time.

Twelve inbound ACH transfers from twelve distinct source accounts converge on 80145D800 between 2022/09/04 and 2022/09/08, totaling roughly 3.7 million USD including a single 3.51 million inflow (T1614), with no outflow from that account in the set. This is consistent with a collection or sink account, but it could also be a legitimate merchant or payroll account, so KYC and business-purpose review of 80145D800 is needed before any conclusion.

Two accounts (8085F5660 and 80827DA70) send 16 transfers in total to 808C30740, which never pays anything out in this window, and the same fixed amounts recur (80.5, 103.85, and 79.46/7626.46/2224.09 on both 09/02 and 09/09), many at off-hours. This consolidation shape fits a fan-in, but it is equally consistent with a legitimate recurring-payment collector, and no cycle, chain, or layering is visible, so the bank should check 808C30740's outflows and the counterparties' KYC before acting.

Funds move D (800EE90B0) to C (800EF5CE0) for $22.1M (T0414), then C sends $4.87M to A (8029FC480) (T0303, T0308). A then splits outflows across B (T0031, T0092, T0156) and E (T0512-T0514, including a $677K cash leg) within hours, with no return to origin, so the pattern is a pass-through chain with a fan-out, not a cycle. The visible slice is small, the ring label is a referral for review rather than a conclusion, and C's smaller payments to F (T0733) and G (T2638) are not flagged because they look unrelated in amount and scale.

No transfer is a self-transfer and no money returns to its origin, so there is no cycle, chain, or scatter-gather. The traffic is mostly repeated fixed-amount transfers between the same pairs (80A95F9F0 to 80AA72E10 and 80AA72BA0 to 80AD21FA0), which look like recurring payments, though 80AA72E10 receives from several senders and never pays out, and that fan-in pattern is worth monitoring.

Account 8000AEDD0 receives seven large AUD transfers from seven different accounts between 2022-09-09 and 2022-09-13 (T2485, T2528, T2714, T2775, T2787, T2792, T2795), then disperses funds in EUR and USD to four different accounts between 09-13 and 09-16 (T2794, T2821, T2823, T2824), a gather-then-disperse pass-through pattern. T1587, T1754 and T1902 also send out of this hub but predate the inflow cluster, so I have not flagged them; the pattern could also reflect legitimate treasury or payment-processing activity, so this needs investigation of the counterparties rather than a conclusion.

Two source accounts (800DA42F0 and 8015A1170) send 16 small transfers to 803158350 over about two weeks, repeating the same amounts (261.35, 120.47, 90.69, 46.62) across the same bank pair, often in late-night bursts. This is consistent with structured fan-in, but the repetition could also be a legitimate recurring payment, so it needs investigation before any conclusion. T1387, T0422 and T2085 are excluded because they do not involve 803158350; T2085 (5612.14 from 8015A1170 to 8078D8C50) is a large outflow that warrants separate review.

Account 800122600 is a busy hub with many small outbound payments to distinct payees (a fan-out shape), but the amounts are modest and varied, the outflows are far smaller than its large inbound transfers from 8000677F0 (T0341, T0344, T2668), and no transfers return funds to the origin, so no clear layering loop or pass-through is visible. The repeated identical amounts (T2018/T2256, T1820/T2357, T1382/T2409) and the duplicated 144713.73 transfer (T0344/T2668) are worth a duplicate-payment or recurring-payment check, but they do not on their own establish laundering.

Account 8000FFBD0 sends 16 transfers to about 10 distinct payees, including large cash and cheque amounts (e.g., T1029/T1031 to 80124B6F0 six minutes apart), which fits a fan-out pattern. Many small, repeated amounts and the absence of any return flow or cycle leave plausible benign explanations such as payroll or vendor payments, so this warrants review rather than a conclusion.

The repeated identical transfers (T0518/T0696/T1376/T1761/T2040/T2243/T2625 from 809305B70 to 809560410, and the 95.93/47.42 pairs from 8090E7E90 to 8093070F0) look like recurring standing payments rather than layering: no funds return to their origin and no multi-hop cycle appears. The 16310.27 ACH from 809305B70 to 809305E30 (T2348) is the largest amount in the set and is worth a routine look at source of funds, but it is a single transfer whose onward leg (T0713, 2628.27) does not match it, so I would not classify the neighborhood as a ring on this evidence.

Account 808556F40 receives only about 2.5k in inbound transfers (T0746, T2366, T1960) but sends about 110k out in repeated identical amounts to 80FB78560 (including a 42,745.25 cash transfer) and 8088B1490, a large outflow-to-inflow mismatch typical of a pass-through account. The repeated amounts and the near-identical sequences on 2022/09/02 and 2022/09/09 could also reflect duplicated or synthetic records, and the source of the outbound funds is unexplained, so this needs source-of-funds review before any conclusion.

Account 8039B1E10 sends 13 outbound transfers to three counterparties, repeating identical amounts (e.g., 739.29, 592.83, 1335.66, 548.82, 396628.48) across many dates and mixed payment formats (cash, cheque, card, wire), and it receives large sums from 800073130 (T2530, T2531, T2650) and 803FA7F90 (T2285) before dispersing them. This is a suspicious dispersal pattern, but it is based on structure alone, so a customer-level review of the 800073130 relationship and the counterparties' business purposes is needed before any conclusion.

The repeated fixed-amount transfers (203.41 to 806D28C60, 180.06 from 8023DDE90, 56.26 to 8062FAC00, 455.16 to 806D28C60) look like recurring payments, and no money returns to its origin, fans out to many, or is gathered back together. T0460 and T0461 (801853DC0 to 805F9C820, 3,099.22 by card and 25,947.76 in cash one minute apart) are the only notable outliers, but a single source with two inbound payments does not establish a scheme, so they warrant a manual check of the cash source and the customer's profile rather than a ring finding.

Account 1004286A8 sends about 26 outbound transfers in roughly 10 days to many different counterparties and banks, including one 104,885.29 cash payment (T2532), with no visible flow returning funds to it, which is a fan-out shape. This is weak evidence: the activity could be ordinary high-volume payments, the two transfers T1193 and T2204 that loop back to hub 8000FFBD0 are equal in amount and do not form a cycle, and the duplicate-amount transfers (T0741/T1859, T0273/T1946, T1188/T2164) look more like recurring payments, so a human review of the counterparties is needed before any conclusion

No cycle, no self-transfers, and no money returns to its origin. The repeated identical amounts from 80EBF45D0 (T0652, T2324: 163.29) and 80EBF4360 (T0729, T2450: 204.24) look like recurring regular payments. Account 80EBF1580 does fan out to 80EBF1FD0, which then fans out to three accounts, and it sends two large ACH transfers (T2428: 32,875.56; T2555: 2,681.32) that are far larger than its small inbound credits. Those are worth a manual review of the recipients and the source of funds, but this extract alone does not show layering or a closed loop, so I would not call it a ring.

Account 8013FD400 is a high-volume hub, and several amounts repeat exactly (for example 1327.39 three times, 575.68 three times), which looks more like recurring bills or payroll than laundering; no transfer returns funds to their origin, so there is no cycle. Account 805E91C70 passes most of T0591 and T1693 onward to new accounts (T0843, T1127) within a day or two, which could be layering, so it is worth a manual look, but six transfers over a week with no structuring below the threshold and no cycle is not enough to call a ring.

Account 8124B1D90 receives inbound transfers from three senders, including a 759,431.76 cheque from 80FE8D220, and forwards large sums (T0037, T0151) to 813189150, which fits a collection-and-forward layering pattern. However, the repeated identical amounts (277.01, 847.44, and small credit-card payments) look more like recurring standing payments than structured layering, and the data gives no sign of value returning to origin, so this should be reviewed rather than treated as confirmed laundering.

Between 9/10 and 9/14, account 80CEC5700 disperses large sums (several in Brazil Real, Shekel, Euro, CAD, USD) to seven intermediaries, and each intermediary forwards funds to 8029FC480 within days, often in similar amounts (e.g., T2771 19537.97 is forwarded unchanged in T2799 and T2800). That split-then-gather pattern fits layering, but the ring is inferred from amounts and timing only, with no account-holder data, and the earlier 8029FC480 transfers (T0308, T0512, T0513) and the repeated identical small transfers (e.g., 792.52 and 5651.41) are unexplained and not flagged.

T0290, T0291 and T0292 are three ACH inflows to 80C988190 within 18 minutes, which is a small fan-in but has no visible onward movement. The 8034A5880 to 80C988190 transfers (T0339 through T2603) are 14 recurring payments of the same two amounts (126.02 cheque, 65.12 credit card) with no return flow or layering, which looks more like a recurring payment arrangement than a laundering network. Review the timing and the odd-hour pairs if other data is available, but these transfers alone do not establish a scheme.

Eleven transfers from 11 distinct accounts all land in 80919B570 within about 28 minutes (11:01 to 11:29), with varied amounts from C$371 to C$6,063 and senders spread across several banks, which is a fan-in shape. Confidence is only medium because this window shows no outflow from 80919B570, no amounts clustered under a reporting threshold, and no visible follow-on movement, so a legitimate collection or payment-aggregation account is still a plausible explanation that needs checking against the account's profile.

The 17 transfers from 8027405D0 to 806E72870 (T0345 through T2727) are a single repeated pair with fixed amounts of 100.0 and 144.6, which is unusual regularity but shows no fan-out, fan-in, or multi-hop return, and the inflows total about 2,056.80. The 806E72870 cash payout of 5,057.06 to 80EFE0000 (T0300) exceeds that inflow and cannot be reconciled from this set, so it merits a source-of-funds check, but it does not establish a layering pattern on its own.

Seven distinct senders each pay large Yen ACH amounts (about 1.2M to 4.6M) to hub 80F5778D0 within about 18 minutes on 2022/09/08, a burst consistent with collection or mule fan-in. The repeated identical-amount transfers from 80F577AF0 (T0852, T2413) and 80F576450 (T1030, T2539) look more like recurring payments, so I have left them out; the activity could still be a legitimate business collecting receipts, so this needs review of the hub account's profile before any conclusion.

The neighborhood is mostly repeated same-amount payments from 800177290 to 80DC8F380 (T0479, T1046, T1374, T1569, T1572, T1840, T2051, T2056, T2547) and 800055A70 to 800106D00 (T1699, T1700, T2061, T1068), which look like recurring payments rather than layering, and there is no return path that closes a cycle. The two identical 144713.73 cheques from 8000677F0 to 800122600 (T0344, T2668) and the large inflows to hub 800122600 are worth a duplicate-posting or source-of-funds check, but they do not show a fan-out, fan-in, or cycle pattern on their own.

Account 800957210 sends large sums (about 13.9k to 19.4k USD or EUR) to six intermediaries over 2 to 4 Sep, and each intermediary forwards a similar amount to 80054CAB0 within about 1 to 3 days (for example T1247 15,968 then T1507 15,265; T0996 18,570 then T1377 22,837). This split-and-regather pattern is consistent with layering, but the synthetic data gives no direct evidence of intent, and the forwarding amounts do not match exactly, so this needs review of the customers' stated purposes before any action.

Account 800093C80 is a high-volume sender (15 transfers to 5 counterparties), but the repeated identical amounts to the same payees (e.g., 8126.58, 30332.68, 1385.46) look like recurring payments rather than structuring, and nothing flows back or reconverges, so no cycle, chain, or gather step appears. Worth a routine review of the 30332.68 and 8126.58 payees, but this neighborhood does not show a laundering pattern on its face.

Funds move in one direction: E and F feed D (T0401, T1547, T1534), D repeatedly sends identical 71,020.50 amounts to A (T0672, T1192, T1430, T1566, T2724), and A disperses repeatedly to B and C at fixed amounts (20,400.53 and 13,706.74 and others), with no return to the origin, so it reads as layering through a pass-through hub rather than a cycle. The repeated identical amounts and off-hours timestamps are unusual, but could be recurring-payment or synthetic-data artifacts, so this warrants review rather than a conclusion of laundering.

Account 80AD40250 receives repeated transfers from 80A6EA1C0 and 80A190110, then sends the identical 41915.85 AUD amount to 80B2988C0 at another bank five times in one week (T0258, T0936, T1579, T1824, T2137). The repeated identical amounts could be ordinary standing payments, and no return cycle is visible, so this warrants review rather than a conclusion. T1083 (0.85 from 80DEFE1D0 to 80AD40250) and the large USD transfers from 80DEFE1D0 (T2569, T2575) are not clearly linked to this cluster and are excluded.

Three source accounts all send to 8113348B0 (fan-in): 810C151B0 makes 14 repeated transfers of only two fixed amounts (1935.12 cash, 1346.02 cheque) over Sept 1-10, often late at night, and 800948490 sends two large one-off amounts (147,088.38 and 410,132.05) on Sept 2. No onward movement from 8113348B0 appears in this set, so this may be a collection or recurring-payment account rather than a laundering layer, and it needs the account's full history and customer profile before any escalation.

Most flows are repeated identical amounts between fixed pairs (e.g., 80F125F30 to 80F5D4A80 at 291.05 and 99.18; 80F181A50 to 80FA97F90 at 103.88), which looks like recurring payments rather than layering, and there is no cycle or return flow. Watch items that do not establish a scheme: account 100428978 fans out to several counterparties including two 4639.58 transfers (T1268, T2333), and T2299 is a 0.01 payment into 80F181A50, a possible account-validation probe, so a review of those counterparties is reasonable.

The dominant feature is 13 repeated transfers from 8006D7690 to 800A57E80 in fixed amounts (33.09 by cheque, 245.1 by credit card) over nine days, which looks more like recurring payments than layering. 800A57E80 does forward funds to 80718C320 (T0989) and 8011F14E0 (T1838), and receives cash from 8006A8A40 (T1740), so it is a possible pass-through hub, but the amounts are modest and nothing cycles back to origin, so the evidence does not support a ring. Reviewing 800A57E80's onward flows and the source of the cash deposit would resolve this.

The transfers form no multi-hop flow: no money returns to its origin, passes onward through intermediaries, or is split and regathered, and 808556EF0 receives from only two senders. The repeated identical amounts from 8012B9F10 to 808556EF0 (3009.38 and 1266.16, recurring on 09/01, 09/02, 09/05, 09/06, 09/08 and 09/09, some at night) are worth a review of recurring-payment context, but they do not match any listed laundering pattern.

Several accounts (80CF53050 repeatedly, plus 80CCB0B70 and 80D68DCA0) funnel transfers into 80CEC5700, which then forwards very large sums (T0087, T0168) to 80DB7F700, a funnel-and-forward pattern. The repeated identical amounts from 80CF53050 (407.32 and 5651.41) and the unusually large Brazil Real outflows are suspicious, but the amounts may be a data-scale artifact, and the pattern alone does not prove laundering, so this needs review of customer and counterparty context.

The data shows a two-hop flow (8008A3EF0 to 8023ED8B0 to 804243320) plus a separate feed into 804243320 from 8006CD860, but there is no return flow or cycle. Inflows to 8023ED8B0 (about 8,071) far exceed its outflows (about 2,107), so it does not look like a pass-through, and the repeated identical amounts fit recurring bills or payroll. The overnight timing of some transfers from 8008A3EF0 is worth a follow-up review, but the evidence does not establish a laundering pattern.

The dominant flow is 80400E7F0 repeatedly sending identical small amounts (25.64 and 118.37) to 80E16D0B0, which looks like recurring payments, with some same-timestamp duplicates (T1020/T1021, T1968/T1969) worth a data-quality check. Nothing in the set moves money onward from 80E16D0B0, and there is no cycle, chain, or mesh, so this is not a clear laundering ring. The single 27,597,606.23 ACH from 80B0A1D70 (T0141) to 80E16D0B0 is unusually large and merits a source-of-funds review, but it is an isolated transfer with no visible layering.

The 14 transfers from 80AA72BA0 to 80AD21FA0 (T0859 through T2338) repeat only two fixed amounts (3569.09 and 12945.86) over about a week, which looks like a recurring commercial payment or duplicate posting rather than layering. The remaining transfers (T0528, T0685, T0723, T1103) show no fan-out, fan-in, cycle, or chain that would support a laundering finding. I'd recommend a routine check of the repeated pair for duplicate postings, not a suspicious-activity referral.

B's outflow to C (about 695) far exceeds what it received from A (about 46), so the flows do not clearly pass the same money along, and the regular amounts may reflect ordinary recurring payments. The 3.54M cheque and 22,955.85 card transfer from 8000F2320 to 800D8D9B0 (T1177, T1185) and the 48.55 transfer to 800718570 (T1538) are not part of this loop and need separate review for a possible fan-out or la

No cycle, fan-in/fan-out ring, or multi-hop layering is evident: the 80A3DE9A0 to 80A4A6D80 set (T0785, T0790, T0794, T0796) and its near-identical repeat on 2022/09/09 (T2382, T2384, T2387, T2389) look like duplicated or replayed records rather than laundering, and the two-hop path 80A3DECB0 to 80A3DE9A0 to 80A4A6D80 (T2252 then T2382-T2389) has no matching amounts or tight timing. The repeated same-amount transfers (also T0886/T1775) are a data-quality or replay concern to check against the source ledger, not evidence of a scheme.

The repeated identical large Yuan transfers from 8035765E0 to 8037FE4C0 and the hub activity at 8035765E0 merit a look at the account's source of funds, but the data alone does not establish a laundering scheme.

T2408 feeds 811BE9820 from 100428A08, adding a chain component, but the pattern is only moderately clear, and the hub's outflows T1702 and T1949 and the separate T2608 are not included because their role is unclear.
